heading: Jump past duplicates instantly
body:
Track the **last index** of each character in a dict. When you hit a duplicate, move your left pointer **past the previous occurrence** in one hop—no need to shrink incrementally.

**Trick:** `start = max(start, state[char] + 1)` ensures the window never moves backward.

heading: When to use variable window
body:
Use a **variable-length sliding window** when you need to find the longest (or shortest) valid substring and the window size isn't fixed.

**Pattern:** expand right, then contract left **only when** you violate a constraint (here: duplicate characters).

label: Crux · Python

q: Why do we use `start = max(start, state[s[end]] + 1)` instead of just `start = state[s[end]] + 1`?
options: To ensure start never moves backward when the duplicate is outside the current window
To handle edge cases where the string is empty
To optimize the time complexity from O(n²) to O(n)
To prevent index out of bounds errors
explain: The max() ensures start only moves forward. If the previous occurrence is before the current window, we don't move start backward.
